literature_notes: All four ledger lines (L1–L4) describe C-terminal tag fusions on ELFN1 — Venus (L1, L2), myc (L3), and GFP via pEGFPN1 (L4) — appended after the last residue of the intracellular domain (residue 828) or at truncation junctions within the intracellular domain (Δ439 through Δ734). ELFN1 is a type-I single-pass transmembrane protein with its C-terminus (residues 439–828) entirely intracellular. No ledger line reports a tag on the extracellular domain (residues 28–417) or at the mature N-terminus (residue 28). The extracellular domain is a large leucine-rich repeat ectodomain, but no insertion into it is evidenced by any ledger line. Zero extracellular surface tag sites are supported.

literature_other_positions.note: Venus fused at the intracellular C-terminus of full-length ELFN1 (ELFN1-Venus); construct traffics to membrane but tag faces the cytoplasm.
myc tag appended at the intracellular C-terminus of full-length ELFN1 (ELFN1-myc); used as backbone for all truncation constructs.
C-terminal GFP fusion via pEGFPN1 on full-length mouse Elfn1; tag is intracellular.
ELFN1Δ439-Venus truncates the intracellular domain entirely and fuses Venus at the TM/intracellular boundary (residue 438, last TM residue); tag remains on the cytoplasmic face.
